newsitem.title: FRANCE: UAP hampered by low profitability - analysts.
newsitem.headline: UAP hampered by low profitability - analysts.

text.p: Low profitability at French insurer Union des Assurances de Paris (UAP) limits potential gains in the shares and made it an unlikely target for a takeover by rival Axa, analysts said on Thursday.

UAP shares surged 3.29 percent on Wednesday on rumours of a public offer from Axa, which Axa denied, and again rose on Thursday thanks to gains in the stock of Banque Nationale de Paris (BNP), in which UAP holds about 14 percent.
UAP closed on Thursday up 1.45 percent at 105 francs on hefty volume of 1.18 million shares. The stock has fallen nearly 20 percent since the start of the year.
"The market is looking for a reason to push the share. At 100 francs, people thought it was a low point, which explains the speculation yesterday," said Guy Akovi, analyst at brokerage Oddo.
UAP's potential to rise is limited to 110 francs per share, he said. He has forecast a first-half net profit of 800 million francs and 1.5 billion for the full year.

The insurer, headed by Jacques Friedmann, made a 1995 first-half net attributable profit of 806 million francs but posted a 1995 year loss of 2.05 billion francs due to massive 4.5 billion francs in provisions in the second half.
UAP publishes first-half results on October 9.

"The shares clearly rose on the rumours, but that seems a bit exaggerated," said a second analyst. "Despite the fall in the share (in recent months) UAP represents 30 billion francs, which would be hard for Claude Bebear (Axa chairman) to swallow, even if he says has a warchest of the same amount."
Beside the takeover rumour, which had circulated iin July when the share was last below 100 francs, analysts point to UAP's weak profitability.

UAP's big problem is the low profitability of its foreign subsidiaries, which it bought at high prices. Colonia in Germany makes a return of 13 percent on capital but after writing down goodwill, that drops to four percent, one analyst said.

"UAP has a level of profitability of five percent, I do not see how they will do better in the future, the areas for improvement are limited," said one analyst who forecast first-half profit of 800 million francs.

Another analyst, who has forecast 850 million for the first half and 1.5 billion for full year, believes the net asset value per share published by UAP of 158 francs was a "bit optimistic." He thinks the figure should be around 130 francs.
UAP is hampered by weak management but has solid assets, although the arrival of Dominique Bazy at the head of UAP France gave grounds for hope, said analysts.

The group has been weakened by international expansion where it has spent 45 billion francs, as well as property problems at its Banque Worms unit. Its French life insurance business is also mediocre.

The group's potential profitability is estimated at three or four billion francs, said one analyst, stripping out tax and its banking problems. He estimated first-half profit would be 700 million francs and full-year results of 1.5-1.6 billion.
